newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Arab insurance premiums set to double to $10 bln.
newsitem.headline: Arab insurance premiums set to double to $10 bln.

text.p: Income from insurance premiums in the Arab world are set to double to $10 billion in the next 14 years, an official at the Arab Insurance Group (ARIG) said.
ARIG underwriter Khalid Rehman also forecast that the Gulf region would maintain its 35 percent market share in the Middle East insurance industry, an ARIG statement said.
"Arab world insurance premiums are expected to double to $10 billion by the year 2010," Rehman said.
He said the reinsurance ratio was expected to drop to about 25 percent "which would produce reinsurance premiums in the Gulf of about $900 million to $1 billion in about 14 years".
Bahrain-based ARIG is one of the biggest insurers in the Arab world and is equally owned by the governments of Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Libya.
Rehman said average gross premium growth rates of between seven and 10 percent were expected.
A large number of industrial and commercial risks and many small capital-based insurance firms contributed to a favourable reinsurance climate in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC).
"Additionally, reasonably profitable results produced by the GCC which has the added advantage of being a natural, catastrophe-free zone," helped, he said.
The GCC groups Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Oman, UAE and Kuwait.
"Despite the encouraging economic forecast, present trends are showing a soft market and a trying time for reinsurers," Rehman said.
